scenes.title: Why is space silent?
scenes.narration: Movies show explosions booming in space. But would an astronaut really hear one?

scenes.title: Sound needs a medium
scenes.narration: Sound is a mechanical wave. It travels as nearby particles push and pull one another.

scenes.title: A pattern of pressure
scenes.narration: In air, those vibrations create alternating compressions and rarefactions, carrying energy forward.

scenes.title: But space is nearly empty
scenes.narration: In a vacuum, there are too few particles to carry ordinary sound waves from place to place.

scenes.title: You need a path to hear
scenes.narration: Your ear hears vibrations only when a material like air can transmit them to you.

params.note: Matter carries vibrations to your ear

scenes.title: No medium, no sound
scenes.narration: So space isn't silent because nothing happens. It's silent because sound has no medium to travel through.

params.note: A vacuum cannot carry ordinary sound
